title: Conditional kappa refinement: 500-digit enclosures and complete native-proof reuse
body:
Exact conditional saving:

**kappa = 0.**

At submission (2026-10-14 13:30:03 UTC), this exceeded source-pinned PR1875 (`d31827d128197345be2d8d5649f5103abb2759ba`) by approximately **6.066855666120612e-301**, and PR1876's400-digit point by approximately **8.118574691758080e-401**. PR1876 now reports a full finite replay at `6a442373e6127b7e0985d277726bcfd9a16a1f36`, with that same exact point. PR1904 appeared afterward (13:38:26 UTC, head `091ba6e64169230d13285d12563390ea76f44208`) reporting a higher1000-digit point by approximately **2.003359509912251e-500**, with native reuse; this PR therefore makes no current-leading claim. These are extremely small arithmetic refinements of the same paid construction, with no practical speedup claimed. Exact rational comparisons use primary source files.

The package preserves PR1800 (`46d865ab92e58098538b8c5348b6a131c99abf45`) byte-for-byte under `parent/`. Its matching-profile600-digit endpoint operand comes from PR1789 (`2f5f9dbb8b8ce9f9a5f90b234e4b03ca3f4ba87b`). That operand is only a nomination: two separately implemented directed rational/fixed-point series enclosures prove the accepted point on the actually admitted native profile. Both reject an above-root point and a one-count rank48 mutation.

The endpoint gaps, r0 and layout slack are `10^-500`, epsilon is `1-2*10^-500`, beta is `1-6*10^-500`, stop is `10^-510`, and the final rational uses a `10^600` floor and `10^-550` backoff. All slacks remain positive; epsilon=1 is rejected. The main row still limits this family to the unchanged supplier's moment root.

Reproduce with Python3.12+, NumPy2.3.5, SymPy1.14.0 and mpmath1.3.0:

```
python -B research/fine-prime-slack500/verify_refinement.py --main "$PWD" --work /absolute/absent/work --jobs 2 --timeout-seconds 1800
```

The portability adapter preserves every frozen parent byte and runs the unchanged parent checker code in an authenticated execution copy. Only CRLF/LF bytes in the two generated parent JSON ledgers and their two manifest digest entries may change. Full-byte comparisons retain every other byte, including mathematical values, JSON types, ordering and whitespace. Both original and execution inventories are checked before and after. The refined ledgers use the same strict newline-only comparison. Format/mathematical-payload mutation controls run with normal and optimized Python. Runtime portability receipts and both regenerated ledgers are retained as CI artifacts.

Default verification is cold and does not reuse native results. The dedicated workflow runs this command on Python3.12 and3.13, requires all committed sources unchanged, and preserves proof receipts and logs. Hosted CI must be checked at the final published head; local PASS is not a hosted-CI claim.

Local evidence was obtained in two source-bound stages. First, the complete fresh native parent and an earlier105-slack point passed in **1181.734seconds** on Windows/CPython3.12.14, with all397 inputs unchanged, four complete complex native word chains, owner reconstruction, invoice,47 supplier inequalities and all required control chains. A separate AI-agent audit authenticated that actual execution. The updated500-point verification then passed in **8.282seconds**, including new57 strict inequalities,17 reason-matched controls, both new actual-profile enclosures and the exact broad-shift guard. It reused that finite native evidence only after authenticating every one of397 baseline source files and1199 execution files, before and after the new checks, under the hard-pinned reviewed seal. This reuse is explicit in the receipt; it is not described as a second native replay. The fresh run had an8GiB aggregate Job Object limit/four-CPU affinity; the new stage had2GiB/two CPUs and used about69.5MB. All400 final package files remained unchanged.

The independent Gaussian guard repairs an inherited vacuous `or True` row: the shifted constant is `d^2-d^2/L`, not the inherited plus sign. Three exact identities and four mathematical mutation controls pass. Parent bytes and notices remain frozen. The bit supplier is PR589 cited unchanged and repriced, not a fresh rebuild of its bit circuit.

The conclusion remains conditional on the inherited compiler, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting, semantic precision, fixed-tape/prime-packing, interchange, recovery, analytic transfer, bit H1-H5, fine-prime padding, gauge-free accretive circuit and union-schedule arguments. Finite arithmetic does not prove those uniform statements, a full Lean multiplication theorem, linear time or an unconditional record. The maintainer-selected result is unchanged. Open next questions and exact reuse invalidation are documented in the package README.

Credits: Jeremy Kothe and PR1800/1839 contributors; Rohan Arun and the concurrent PR1828/1875/1876 precision work; midhatn/PR1789's matching-profile operand; Chafik Boukhalfa/PR1786 and Tim Trudgian's prime theorem; Vlado Vojdanovski/PR1673; PR1758 and the complete retained supplier lineage. The source-bound local verification summary is committed at `certificates/fine-prime-slack500-local.json`; the separately reviewed actual500 closure has SHA256 `0dd6face3587680ec64527c533f5a039f883af4961a4b6c4ceea1f73ab0349b1`.

### Clarification of finite cutoff and proof scope — 2026-10-14

**The parent's recorded `bootstrap` and `conservative_bootstrap` `cutoff_log2` values at `PAYLOAD=2048` are fixed-allowance arithmetic samples, not certified thresholds for the actual algorithms including carried constants.** Our source-bound local AI-agent reviews find that 58 of the 60 samples fail the written minimal-carry test. This does not change the numerical κ calculation or disprove the conditional asymptotic bound. The finding follows Rohan Arun's [original PR387 proof mirror, pinned at `0b1cccf8`](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea/research/bootstrap-depth-audit/sources/pr387/PROOF.md) and Josie Elliston's [PR1956 audit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1956).

Under the inherited **uniform all-size, completed-algorithm, stopped-construction, stock-fit and paid compiler premises**, stage-dependent dominating constants and sufficiently large finite cutoffs can instead be chosen sequentially: fix the previous algorithm, then the stopped procedure and its uniform thresholds, then the current cutoff, then the next completed time constant. This preserves the same fixed-depth exponent recurrence; it does not certify the stored samples, assert actual `2^2048` bounds, or supply a numerical cutoff certificate. Josie Elliston's [PR1965](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1965) discusses a separate stock/time absorption repair.

[PR1964-based extended-label checks](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1964) pass for both providers and orientations and reject scalar-neutral X/Y/Z adapter controls; H2 and all-size obligations remain inherited. These are AI-agent reviews, not independent human peer review. This clarification supplies no new theorem, frontier result, source change or native replay.
